subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.j@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alice — great conversation. Quick recap and the set of next steps we discussed so we can align internally and get you a defensible TCO/ROI for the pilot.

Key pain points you called out:
- High inference run-rate and unpredictable per-request cost (spiked in Q3).
- Tight latency SLOs for the customer-facing search/assistant (target 100ms P95).
- Strict annual budget target for new AI projects (~$100k/yr for initial pilot).

Goals from the call:
- Demonstrate a path to ~50–70% reduction in inference spend vs current vendor while meeting latency targets.
- Validate that batching + KV/prefix caching can reduce token volume and average compute per request without regressions in quality.
- Put together a 3-month pilot plan with clear metric gates (cost per 1k tokens, P95 latency, API error rate).

High-level TCO levers we discussed (and assumptions used in the attached spreadsheet):
- Workload: ~200M tokens/month (current).
- Baseline vendor cost: ~$0.30 / 1K tokens (current contract) → ~$60k/mo (extrapolated).
- Redwood pilot config: quantized LLM variant + batching + prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts → expected cost ~ $0.08 / 1K tokens (conservative estimate) given compute and batching assumptions.
- Estimated savings: ~3–4x reduction in per-token spend; combined with caching (we estimate 15–30% token reduction on your query patterns) results in ~60% cost reduction overall in pilot scenarios.

Notes on how we get there technically:
- Batching: we’ll use dynamic request batching for background jobs and a low-latency micro-batching path for interactive traffic to keep P95 within 100ms.
- KV/prefix caching: for repeated prompts (session-based queries) we expect to avoid re-computing prefixes for ~20–35% of the tokens depending on your session patterns.
- Quantization / model choice: switching to a 4-bit quantized model variant reduces GPU memory and can lower instance type costs; we’ll validate any quality delta on your eval set.
- Fallbacks: if a higher-quality model is needed for a subset of traffic, we can route (canary) 10% of requests to the larger model and measure ROI.

Attached: ACME_Redwood_TCO_Estimate_v1.xlsx (tabbed for baseline vs pilot scenarios) and a sample metrics export placeholder (acme-sample-inference-metrics.json) you can replace with logs.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send the 2–4 day sample of request logs (or the metrics export we referenced) so we can run an exact TCO projection against your distribution.
2) Schedule a 30–45m technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer (Tom) and our solutions engineer Rafael to validate latency/architecture constraints.
3) We deliver an updated TCO + pilot plan (including SLOs, rollout gating, and estimated credits) by next Wednesday (11/24).

Are you available for a technical deep-dive on Thu 11/19 10:30–11:00am PT or Fri 11/20 9:00–9:45am PT? Rafael will join.

Thanks — I’ll circulate the spreadsheet now.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: Alice Johnson <alice.j@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Thanks, Marissa — good writeup and aligns with what I captured. A couple quick clarifications before we send logs over:

1) Our current "200M tokens/mo" number is a peak estimate across combined search + assistant traffic. Normalized steady-state is closer to 120–140M tokens/mo; we want both baseline and peak in the sheet.
2) Budget: the $100k/yr is for the first-phase pilot (proof-of-value) — if we hit the 60% savings target we can expand spend into next year. So having both monthly and annualized ROI lines is key.
3) Latency: 100ms P95 is a hard req for the assistant (search can tolerate 200–300ms). If micro-batching risks pushing P95 above 120ms we need an express path.

I'm attaching a small sample (anonymized) of our request histogram and a short CSV of prompt lengths — should give you a better distribution to run caching estimates on.

Can you confirm the conservative cost per 1K tokens ($0.08) includes instance amortization and expected batching gains? Also please call out any one-time migration/engineering effort that should be included in the pilot TCO.

If it helps, Thu 11/19 10:30am PT works for Tom and me.

Best,
Alice

[Attachment: acme-sample-inference-metrics.json]
